stage: pilot-0: merge four EXISTING adapters on one base model; no training

backend.note: The pure-Python CPU reference in src/ cannot handle 768x768 layers; a numpy/torch port of wrrr/minimax must be cross-checked against the pure-Python reference on small matrices before use.

base_model.license_reported: Apache-2.0 (HF model card, read by a web-reading subagent)

asset_verification_notes: declared_base read from adapter_config.json on the web for cola and rte only (per subagent); mrpc and sst2 UNVERIFIED
no adapter repo carries a license tag (per subagent); usage terms must be confirmed with the publisher
adapter training split and checkpoint-selection data UNVERIFIED: if GLUE validation was used for selection, our dev/test (drawn from validation) are contaminated
Flan-T5 was instruction-tuned on GLUE-like tasks, so base-model headroom may be small

code.evaluation_prompts: FusionBench flan-t5 GLUE templates (github.com/tanganke/fusion_bench, MIT reported)

datasets.license_reported: per-subset original licenses; SST-2 'Unknown' on HF card

test.use: reported once, after all choices are frozen

splits.disjointness: calibration (train) is disjoint from dev/test (validation) by construction; dev and test are disjoint halves

task_identity_disclosure.merging_task_identity_detail: per-task calibration Grams / functional errors require knowing which calibration inputs belong to which task (same for RegMean-family baselines)
task_identity_disclosure.inference_task_identity_detail: task-specific prompt template and label words (shared LM head); no task-specific heads

merge_scope.modules: every LoRA-targeted linear (q, v) in encoder self-attn, decoder self-attn and decoder cross-attn
merge_scope.activation_source: each task's own fine-tuned model (base + adapter_t) on task-t calibration inputs (RegMean convention)
merge_scope.activation_source_ablation: merged-model previous-layer activations (RegMean++ convention), ablation only
merge_scope.effective_delta: dW_t = (lora_alpha / r) * B_t @ A_t; factors are never merged directly

rank_budget.note: every method is truncated/constrained to the same final rank per layer; methods that exceed it are reported separately and never ranked against rank-matched methods

individual_adapter_t.final_rank: r per task (oracle upper reference; uses 4x parameters and task routing)

knots_ties_trunc.final_rank: k (KnOTS itself has no rank budget; truncation is ours)
knots_ties_trunc.implementation: official KnOTS code preferred; unofficial re-implementation must be labelled

ctm.implementation: official code if released (UNVERIFIED); otherwise unofficial ctm_like_ta, labelled

solver.wrrr_mode: pd, falling back to pinv (same objective) when S is singular; ridge never used for bounds

primary_metric: test worst-task normalized accuracy: min_t acc_t(merged) / acc_t(adapter_t alone), rank-matched methods only
secondary_metrics: test worst-task and mean absolute accuracy
layer-level worst-task relative functional error on test inputs (diagnostic only; never a success criterion)

minimum_effect_of_interest.comparator: best rank-matched baseline with the SAME calibration access, selected on dev (not test)
minimum_effect_of_interest.decision: effect must exceed MEI in mean over seeds AND in at least 3 of 3 seeds; otherwise NOT_SUPPORTED

resource_caps.note: caps are limits, not measured spend; actual wall time and peak memory are recorded per run

stopping_rules: If minimax_rel improves only the layer-level functional error but not the primary metric by >= MEI: stop; do not expand scope.
If an advantage appears only with more rank, more calibration data or more compute than the comparator: stop automatic expansion and report.
If the calibration duality gap is not small, report UB/LB and do not describe the solution as optimal.
Any FAILED/OOM/NOT_RUN condition is preserved in the run log; skipped cells are not counted as passes.
